FOREWORD

0.-1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 31 October 1967, after the draft finalized by the Pest Control Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council and the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 Endosulfan dusting powders containing varying percentages of .endosulfan, technical, are largeJy used in the control of pests of agricultural importance. 0.3 Taking into consideration the views of producers, consumers.. testing authorities and technologists, the Sectional Committee responsible for the preparation of this standard felt that it should be related to the manufacturing and trade practices followed in the country in this field. 0.4 This standard is one of a series of Indian Standards on pesticides and their formulations.

0.5 This standard contains cIa uses 3.1, E-2.3 and E-3.4 which call for an
agreement between the purchaser and the vendor. 0.6 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of.this _standard. is complied with, the final value, ?b~~ryed or ~al~

[ Table 1, Item (i) ]
DETERMINATION OF XNDOSULFAN CONTENT

A-I. PRINCIPLE OF THE METHOD A-t.l The principle in determination of endosulfan is based on hydrolysis of endosulfan with methanolic sodium hydroxide and estimating the sodium sulphite ( Na,sO.) formed iodimetricaUy_
A-2. REAGENTS

A-2.1 Metba.o)
A-2.1 Sodium Hydroxide Pelletl
A-2.3 PbeaolpbtlaaJela IndlClltor Solatlo. - one percent (wi') in rectified spirit ( conforming to IS : 323-19S9t).

A-1.. Staadard Salpbarlc Acid - S N_
A-2.5 Stanurd IodiDe Solation - 0-1 N-

A�2-6 Sta.dan! Sodium Tblosa)pbate SoJ.tio. - 0-1 N.

A-2.'1 Starch ladle-tor sol .. 108 - 0-2 percent, freshly prepared.

A-3. PROCEDURE
A-3.1 Weigh accurately a quantity or the material containing about 0�5 g of endosulfan, technical, and tranafer it to a 2SO-ml flask. Add 100 ml of methanol by a pipette. Introduce about 1-5 g of sodium hydroxide pellets (about 15 pellet! ). Connect the Bask to a reflux condenser and boil the contents at least for two houri. Shake the flask
�SpecUlcation for water. di.t.il1ed quality ( ml.,I1)t8peoilloatioD for recti8ed apirit ( reviled ).

6

IS : 4.lU -1967
occasionally. Wash down the condenser with 20 ml of methanol and SO ml of distilled water. Add one drop of the phenolphthalein indicator lolution. Neutralize with standard sulphuric acid. Add a few drops.. of dilute sodium hydroxide solution to restore the indicator colour and to prevent any loss of sulphur dioxide. A-3.2 For accurate determination of the sulphite, it is euential to add the sodium sulphite to an excess of acidi&ed standard iodine lolution
and back titrate the excess of iodine with standard sodium thiosulphate solution. A-3.3 Take 40 ml of standard iodine solution in a SQO-ml glass stopper. , ed iodine flask from a. burette. Add 1 ml or the standard sulphuric acid and shake it slowly. While agitating, add the sulphite solution. Rinse the 8alk well with small portions distilled water until all the sulphite has been transferred. (The washing procedure should be continued until there is insufficient sulphite in the Sask to bleach a small drop of iodine.) The final volume in the iodine flalk should be from 225 to 250 mI. A-3." Back titrate the exces. iodine with the Itandard sodium thiosulphate solution uling starch solution as indicator and titrate until the blue colour disappears. A-3.5 Carry out a blank determination by titrating 40 ml of the standard iodine solution with 175 ml of water acldified by I ml of Itandard sulphuric acid with standard sodium thiosulphate solution. A-3.6 The difference in the volume of sodium thiosulphate solution indicates the iodine equivalent consumed by endosulfan,

B-2. PROCEDURE

Two small square rubber cube. are introduced along with the material on the sieve to facilitate the breaking up of any soft lumps of the caked material. After 20 minutes stop the machine and brush the residue on the sieve into a tared weighing dish Weigh the dish and determine the weight of the residue. 8-3. CALCULATION

Weigh the filled cylinder and calculate the bulk density before compacting (weight of the material/volume occupied by the material). APPENDIX E ( Clause 4.1 )
SAMPLING 0 .. ENDOSULFAN DUSTING POWDERS

GENERAL PRECAUTIONS

&-1.0 In drawing, prepar~. storing and handling test sample., the following precautions and directions shall be observed. &-1.1 Samples sban not be taken in an exposed place. Eel.! The lampling instrument shall be clean and dry when used.
11

IS:

en� 1967

E-L3 Proper precautions shall be taken while drawing sample. since
the material is toxic. E-l.4 Precautions shall be taken to protect the aamples, the material being sampled, the sampling instruments and the receptacles for samples from adventitious contamination.

E-l.5 To draw a representative sample, the contents of each container selected for sampling shall be mixed al thoroughly as. possible by shaking or by any other suitable means so al to bring aU portions into uniform distribution.
&-1.6 The samples shall be placed in suitable, clean, dry and air-tight receptacles on which the material has no action.
�-1.7 The sample receptacles shall be of such a size that they are almost, but not complete! y, filled by the sample.

E-I.8 Each sample receptacle shall be sealed air-tight after filling and marked with full details of sampling, date of manufacture, name of the manufacturer and other particulars of the consignment.
E-I.9 Samples shall be stored in such a manner that the temperature of the material does not vary unduly from the normal temperature. E-l.lO Samples shaU be protected from light.

�-2. SCALE OF SAMPLING
&-2.1 Lot - All the container. in a single consignment of the material drawn from the same batch of manufacture shall constitute a lot. If a consignment is declared or it known to consist of different batches of manufacture, the containers belonging to the same batch sball be grouped together and each such group shall constitute a separate lot. E-1.1.1 Samples shall be tested for each lot for ascertaining the conformity of the material to the requirements of this specification.

E-2.1 The number (PI) of containers to be chosen from the lot shall depend on the size of the lot and shan be in accordance with colI and 2 of Table 2. 1:-1.3 These containers shall be chosen at random from the lot and in
order to ensure the randomness of selection, lome random number table
al agreed to 'between the purchaser and the vendor shall be used. In case such a table is not available, the followiDI procedure lhall be

adopted: Starting from any container in the lot. count them as I, ~ 3, etc, up to r in one order. where, is equal to the integral part of the

12

IS : 4.122 � 1961
value N/It, N being the total Dumber of containers in the lot and II the number of containers to be chosen (Table 2). Every rth container thus counted shall be separated until the requisite number of container. is obtained from the lot to give samples for test.

E-3. TFST SAMPLES AND REFEREE SAMPLES E-3.1 Before drawing the test sample, mix thoroughly the contents of each container selected, by shaking or by any other suitable means.
Draw small portions of the material from different parts of each container selected ( Table 2). The total quantity of the material drawn from each container shall be sufficient to conduct the tests for all the characteristics given in Table 1 and shall be not less than 500 g.
.

.

E-3.2 Mix thoroughly all portions of the material drawn from the same container. Out of these portions. a small but equal quantity shall be taken for each selected container and shall be well mixed together so as to form a composite sample of not less than 60 g. This composite sample shall be divided into three equal parts, one for the purchaser, another for the vendor .. nd the third for the referee. E-3.3 The remaining portion. of the material from each container (after a small quantity needed for the formation of the composite sample has been taken out) shall be divided into three equal parts. These parts shall be immediately transfer-red to thoroughly dried sample receptacles which are then sealed air-tight and labelled with all the particulars of sampling given under E-I.I. The material in each such sealed receptacle Ih.;11 constitute a test sample. These individual samples shall be leparated into three identical setl of test samples iD luch a way that each set has a sample representing each container selected ( ~able 2 ). One of these three let! shall be

marked for the purchaser, another for the vendor and the third for the
referee. E-3.4 Referee S � .,les - Referee samples shall consist of the compolite sample (�-3.2) and a set of individual test samples (�.3.3) marked for this purpose and shall bear the seals of the purchaser and the vendor. These shall be kept at a place agreed to between the two.

FA. NUMBER OF TFSTS
E-4.1 Tests for description and the determination of endosulfan content, material passing through 75-micron IS Sieve, and buJk density after compacting shall be conducted individually on each of the samples constituting a set of test samples ( E-3.3 ). E-4.2 Test for the determination of the remaining characteristic, namely, acidity or alkalinity, shall be conducted on the composite sample as prepared under E�3.2.

E-S. CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY
E-5.1

is. lot shall be declared as

conforming to the specification, when:

a) each of the, test results for description, endosulfan content, material passing through 75-micron IS Sieve, and bulk density after compacting satisfies the corresponding requirement specified in Table 1. If, however, one or more of the test results do not satisfy the specified requirements, the conformity of the lot shall be ascertained in accordance with E-~.1.1; and b) the test result on the composite sample for acidity or alkalinity satisfies the corresponding requirement given in Table 1. E-5.1.1 In case one or more of the test results do not satisfy the requirements for endosulfan content, material passing through 7S-micron IS Sieve and bulk density after compacting the following procedure shall be adopted for determining conformity of the rna terial 10 respect of these characteristics. The mean and the range of the corresponding test results shall be calculated as: Mean (X)

=

The sum of the test results Number of test results

Range ( R)

=

The difference between the highest and the lowest
value obtained for the test results.

The appropriate expressions as shown in col 6 of Table 3 shall be calculated. If the values of these expressions safisfy the relevant condition as given in col 6 of Table 3, the lot shall be declared to have
